text:
Aisha: Quick sync — Halcyon POC goes live Mon. They need hosted API keys for 2 engs and security wants a clear rotation + revocation process. Can we outline the recommended flow and what we can hand them for the POC? cc @sam_se @priya_security
Sam_SE: For POC, we usually issue short-lived hosted keys (ephemeral or scoped) rather than long-lived tokens. How long do they need access?
Aisha: 2 weeks of testing but engineers will rotate daily if needed. Security side wants audit trail + ability to revoke immediately.
Luca_Engineering: Recommend this pattern: 1) create scoped ephemeral keys (72h max) 2) provide via 1Password or signed link 3) enable IP allowlist for the key + per-key quota 4) set up an automated rotation cron if they need continuous refresh. Example CLI to create ephemeral key:```
redwood-cli keys create --type ephemeral --expires-in 72h --scope generate,embed --note "halcyon-poc-eng1"```
Priya_Security: +1 to ephemeral. For the security questionnaire, we'll require: - TTL <= 72h (prefer 24h) - rotation logs in Console + exported audit logs to S3/KMS - revocation endpoint documented - principle of least privilege on scopes - IP allowlist and CIDR ranges if possible. Also request that the keys are not embedded in client-side code. :lock:
Sam_SE: Revocation is immediate from Console or CLI:```
redwood-cli keys revoke <key-id>```
We also support programmatic revoke via API POST /v1/keys/<id>/revoke and webhooks to notify teams on rotation/failures. For handshake security, we provide a one-time download link when creating ephemeral keys and a short TTL on that link.
Aisha: Can we automate rotation so Halcyon doesn't have to run cron? They prefer an endpoint we can call to rotate tokens and push to their CI secret store.
Luca_Engineering: Yes — we have a rotate API and a small lambda example in docs. Simple flow: create service account, grant it permission to call /v1/keys/rotate for the key alias, then push the returned secret to Vault/1Password. We'll paste the snippet in the doc.
Infra-bot: Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/keys#ephemeral-keys (internal) — includes CLI, API, and rotation examples. Also shows audit log export config.
Priya_Security: For the security questionnaire answer draft, include: token types, TTL policy, revocation steps, audit export path, recommended least-privilege scopes, and recommended handoff controls (1Password or signed one-time link). I'll review the draft.
Aisha: I'll prepare the credential handoff checklist and the SecQ answers tonight and @priya_security for review. Once approved we'll provision 2 ephemeral keys and share via 1Password. :thumbsup:
Sam_SE: I'll create the keys and set the expiry to 48h for now. Send me the names for the two engineers and their IP CIDRs if they want restrict to their office.
Aisha: Thanks — looping in Halcyon contact separately. Will post the engineer names here when ready.
Priya_Security: One more thing — add a short rotation policy to the POC contract: keys are rotated every 48h and any suspected compromise must be reported to security@redwood.ai immediately.
Aisha: Noted. I'll add that to the POC terms.
Luca_Engineering: If they later request longer-lived keys for integration testing, we can provision dedicated scoped tokens via Dedicated project with RBAC and audit hooks. For the POC stick to ephemeral.
Aisha: Great, thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the checklist + SecQ draft.
